clue.text: A guideline for colours

definitions.meaning: a benchmark or norm that others are measured against
a regiment's colours are its flag, carried on parade

explanation.surface: Someone asks for a reference chart to follow when choosing paint shades.
explanation.definitionFit: A flag carried into battle and a level of quality to be met share one word in English.

clue.text: A meal requiring a little catsup, perhaps

indicators.note: a little says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: An evening dish that needs only a dash of ketchup.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft's definition took in 'requiring', which is only a link word; 'A meal' alone defines. Catsup is an old spelling of ketchup.
explanation.definitionFit: Supper is the evening meal.

clue.text: Making a note to finish a list of things to be seen to

annotationWithheld.why: Making a note to finish a list of things to be seen to: definition is the list, A at the end is a note, but no sound sense of 'Making' gives AGEND (perhaps D is a second note and 'Making' GEN), so the parse cannot be shown honestly
annotationWithheld.clue: Making a note to finish a list of things to be seen to

clue.text: Seaside upset giving rise to complaint

indicators.note: upset means knocked over and disturbed, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A disturbance at the coast leads to someone grumbling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'complaint' looks like a grievance; it means an illness.
explanation.definitionFit: A complaint can be an ailment, a medical sense.

clue.text: The class appears quite exuberant

definitions.meaning: a grade or class in a hierarchy
exuberant growth is lush and overgrown, as weeds are

explanation.surface: The pupils seem very high-spirited.
explanation.definitionFit: A grade in a hierarchy and vegetation growing too lushly share one word.

clue.text: The eccentric is deep, as may well be discerned

indicators.note: something eccentric is off-centre and odd, so these letters are set out in a strange new order

explanation.surface: An odd character turns out to be profound, as could readily be perceived.
explanation.walkthrough: 'eccentric' rearranges the letters of IS DEEP.
explanation.definitionFit: To discern something is to catch sight of it, a plain synonym.

clue.text: A bird's down

definitions.meaning: to down a drink is to gulp it

explanation.surface: The soft feathers belong to a bird.
explanation.definitionFit: A migrating bird and the act of gulping something share one word.

clue.text: Popular river's about dry, and that could be dangerous

parts.note: in means fashionable or popular
sec is French for dry, used of wine
the Ure is a river in Yorkshire

explanation.surface: A well-liked river has nearly run dry, which could be risky.
explanation.walkthrough: The Ure is a river in North Yorkshire, England, a crossword favourite.
explanation.definitionFit: Something unsafe or not firmly fixed is hazardous, a loose synonym.

clue.text: Mark must get up in time to set off

indicators.note: in means the reversed piece goes inside the time word

parts.note: a date is a point in time

indicators.note: get up, in a down clue, means the word is read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: to mark something is to note it

explanation.surface: Someone must rise on schedule to set out.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'get up' turns the mark word so it reads upwards before 'in' places it inside the time word. 'set off' means explode, not depart.
explanation.definitionFit: To set off a bomb is to make it explode.

clue.text: Appealing puff about pasture

indicators.note: about means one word wraps round the other, so the breath word surrounds the meadow word

parts.note: to puff is to pant, gasping for breath
leas are grassy fields used as pasture

explanation.surface: An attractive breath of air drifts over the grazing land.
explanation.walkthrough: Lea is a poetic word for a meadow, often met in crosswords; 'about' wraps the breath word round its plural.
explanation.definitionFit: Something appealing is agreeable or nice to be around.

clue.text: Hound university people joining the party

parts.note: BAs are Bachelors of Arts, graduates of a university
a set is a group or party of people

explanation.surface: Some graduates are pestered into joining a social circle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hound' looks like a verb meaning to pester; it is the dog.
explanation.definitionFit: A basset is a short-legged breed of hunting dog.

clue.text: Church dignitaries never proceeding in a straight forward way

definitions.meaning: senior clergy in charge of dioceses

definitions.text: never proceeding in a straight forward way
definitions.meaning: chess pieces that move only diagonally

explanation.surface: Senior clergy are accused of always being devious.
explanation.definitionFit: Senior clergy and the diagonal-moving chessmen share one name.

clue.text: To win calls for close attention

parts.note: a close is an end or finish
to give someone your ear is to pay them attention

explanation.surface: Victory demands that you concentrate hard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'win' here means to win over or charm someone, as in winning their heart.
explanation.definitionFit: To endear yourself is to win affection, making others fond of you.

clue.text: The boiler William wanted -May too

parts.note: Billy is a familiar form of the name William
may and can both express permission

explanation.surface: William wanted the boiler, and so did a woman called May.
explanation.walkthrough: 'May' poses as a woman's name; it is the verb of permission, a synonym of can.
explanation.definitionFit: A billycan is a tin pot for boiling water over a campfire, used in the Australian bush.

clue.text: One imagines the German article to contain a quantity of paper

indicators.note: to contain means one piece holds the other inside it

parts.note: der is German for the
a ream is 500 sheets of paper

explanation.surface: Someone thinks a German newspaper article fills a stack of pages.
explanation.walkthrough: 'article' looks like a newspaper piece; it is the grammatical article.
explanation.definitionFit: A person lost in fantasy or visions is one who imagines.

clue.text: When there's bad weather with frost, expect trouble

indicators.note: bad suggests the letters have gone wrong and must be put back in a different order

explanation.surface: When storms and frost arrive, a cautious person braces for difficulties.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bad' rearranges WEATHER and FROST together.
explanation.definitionFit: To anticipate the most unpleasant outcome is to brace for difficulty, an idiom.

clue.text: The child preparing to fight could be 9

parts.note: arming is taking up weapons before battle

explanation.surface: The little one getting ready for a scrap might be nice.
explanation.walkthrough: 9 refers to the answer at 9 across, PLEASANT.
explanation.definitionFit: A delightful person is agreeable company, a close synonym of the other answer.

clue.text: An insect's metamorphosis for example

indicators.note: a metamorphosis is a change of form, as when a caterpillar becomes a moth, so the letters change shape

parts.note: the 's only shows possession or stands for 'is', so it adds no letters: the word before it gives these letters as it is written

explanation.surface: An insect transforms, as one illustration.
explanation.walkthrough: 'metamorphosis' rearranges AN INSECT.
explanation.definitionFit: For example and in one case mean the same thing.

clue.text: Acclaim for manual about drinking

parts.note: manual means by hand
C is short for circa, Latin for about
lapping is drinking with the tongue, as a cat does

explanation.surface: Praise for a handbook about drinking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'manual' looks like a noun, a handbook, but stands for HAND.
explanation.definitionFit: Applause made by striking the palms together is a form of acclaim.

clue.text: Copper severely criticises men of the cloth

parts.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper
to rate someone is to scold them severely

explanation.surface: A policeman berates the clergy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Copper' looks like a policeman; it is the metal. Rate is an old verb meaning to scold.
explanation.definitionFit: Assistant parish priests are clergymen, men of the cloth.

clue.text: Exceptional need for basic furniture

definitions.meaning: said of a room lacking even a table to eat at

explanation.surface: An urgent need for basic furnishings.
explanation.definitionFit: Something remarkable is worth noticing, and the phrase splits to say a room lacks a table.

clue.text: The odd rustic may raise such fruit

indicators.note: odd means strange, so the letters are put into an unusual order

explanation.surface: An eccentric countryman might grow oranges.
explanation.walkthrough: 'odd' rearranges RUSTIC.
explanation.definitionFit: Oranges and lemons belong to the citrus family of fruits.

clue.text: Add salt at the appropriate time

definitions.meaning: to flavour food with salt or spices

explanation.surface: Salt the dish at just the right moment.
explanation.definitionFit: Flavouring food and a period of the year suited to something share one word.

clue.text: Returned, finding wrong hiding in the tall grass

indicators.note: hiding in means one piece sits concealed within the other

parts.note: a reed is a tall grass growing in wet places
a tort is a civil wrong in law

explanation.surface: Someone came back, having found a crime concealed among the long grass.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Returned' means answered back, as with a sharp reply, not came back.
explanation.definitionFit: To retort is to reply sharply, so returned a remark.

clue.text: Hit that means everybody's out

definitions.meaning: to hit is to ... a blow
a stoppage where all workers walk out

explanation.surface: A blow that leaves everyone flattened.
explanation.definitionFit: A blow and an industrial walkout share one word.

clue.text: Grasping what tis suggested by 'average'

definitions.meaning: an average is the arithmetic midpoint

explanation.surface: A greedy reading of what average implies.
explanation.definitionFit: Being stingy and the arithmetic average share one word.

clue.text: Make light of this

parts.note: make light of usually means treat lightly, but here it means set alight, so produce light from it

explanation.definitionFit: To set fire to something makes it burn and give out light.

clue.text: They fly across the ocean as brides to be

indicators.note: brides to be are not yet themselves, so their letters are still to be formed into something else

explanation.surface: Future brides fly abroad over the sea for their weddings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be' signals the anagram of AS BRIDES, playing on the phrase brides-to-be.
explanation.definitionFit: Gulls, albatrosses and similar birds range over the open sea.

clue.text: Attractive-sounding rock

indicators.note: sounding says the word is heard rather than read, a homophone

parts.note: nice means pleasant or attractive

explanation.surface: A stone said to be good-looking.
explanation.walkthrough: The G of the rock name is silent.
explanation.definitionFit: Gneiss is a banded metamorphic rock.

clue.text: Irrationality of a Parisian about a certain issue

parts.note: un is French for a
re means concerning or about
a son is one particular kind of issue, or offspring

explanation.surface: A Frenchman's illogical stance on a specific topic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'issue' looks like a topic; it means offspring.
explanation.definitionFit: A lack of logic or sense is irrationality, a near synonym.
